Question_text: A student uses a small plotting compass to investigate the magnetic field due to a bar magnet. The student places a piece of thin card over one end of the magnet, as shown in Fig. 1.1a.
image: Fig. 1.1a shows a 3D perspective of a bar magnet with a thin card placed over one end. Fig. 1.1b (top view) shows the rectangular outline of the thin card with a dashed square representing the 'top of magnet under card' at its center.

Parts.part_text: Describe how the student can use the small plotting compass to plot the shape of the magnetic field on the card. You may draw on Fig. 1.1b if you wish.
Explain why the plotting compass must be small.
Apart from the shape, state what else can be deduced about the magnetic field with this apparatus.

Question_text: A student investigates the use of pulleys to lift a load. The student uses two pulleys A and B to lift a load W, as shown in Fig. 2.1. The student uses a newton meter to measure the minimum force F needed to raise the load.
image: Fig. 2.1 shows a pulley system. Pulley A is fixed to a support. Pulley B is movable and connected to a load W. A string passes over pulley A, then under pulley B, and is pulled by a newton meter (measuring force F). The other end of the string is fixed to the support.

Parts.part_text: Explain why the student uses a constant speed.
Suggest a reason for using a slow constant speed.
State the force F shown by the newton meter.
Parts.image: Fig. 2.2 shows a close-up of a newton meter scale, marked with '0N', '1', and '2'. The pointer indicates a value of 0.6N.

Parts.part_text: On Fig. 2.2, mark the position of the eye of the student when taking the reading.
The student takes a series of readings of F for different values of W. The readings are shown in Fig. 2.3. On Fig. 2.3, write your value of F from (b)(i).
Parts.image: Fig. 2.3 is a table with columns 'W/N' and 'F/N' and several rows of data for force (F) measured for different loads (W). The first row for F/N is blank to be filled.

Parts.part_text: On Fig. 2.4, plot the graph of F/N on the y-axis against W/N on the x-axis. Start your axes from the origin. Draw the straight line of best fit.
Parts.image: Fig. 2.4 is a large, square grid with '0' marked at the bottom-left corner, intended for plotting a graph.

Parts.part_text: Use your graph to find the value of F when W = 0.
Suggest a reason why the line of best fit does not pass through the origin.
Determine the gradient of the line. Show your working. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.

Question_text: A student is given two resistors of resistance 24Ω and 24kΩ. Each resistor is marked with three coloured bands. Fig. 3.1 shows the resistor colour code.
image: Fig. 3.1 is a table showing the resistor colour code, mapping colours (black, brown, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, grey, white) to numerical values (0-9).

Parts.part_text: State the colours of the bands on the resistors given to the student.
Describe in words how the three resistors are combined to give the smallest possible resistance.

Fig. 3.2 shows one possible combination of the three resistors connected between the points A and B. In the three boxes of Fig. 3.3, draw three other possible combinations of all three resistors connected between points A and B.
Parts.image: Fig. 3.2 shows three resistors connected in series between points A and B. Fig. 3.3 shows three empty boxes with points A and B, intended for drawing resistor combinations.

Parts.part_text: The student needs a resistance of 36Ω for his experiment. On Fig. 3.3, mark with the letter E the combination that has this resistance.

Question_text: A student is given a cylindrical 250 cm³ beaker. He is asked to find the outside diameter of the beaker. The other apparatus available is shown below.
image: An 'Apparatus List' table is provided, listing: two half-metre rules, 30 cm ruler, 2m thin string, 2m thick string, plain paper, blocks of wood, marker pen, pencil, scissors, Blu-Tack, Sellotape, lined paper.

Parts.part_text: Describe in detail how the student can obtain an accurate value for the outside diameter of the beaker. In your account you should • state the equipment used, • explain how the equipment is used, • state any readings taken, • explain how the value for the diameter is obtained, • describe how to make the measurement accurate.
Suggest one reason why it is more difficult to measure the internal diameter of the beaker.
